answer: A Sybil carve-out fails when each registered agent must post a per-identity bond that is slashed on proven duplication. To run a thousand puppets, an attacker locks a thousand full stakes at once, and any peer can flag a cedar-like clone by comparing declared histories. The losing bond is destroyed, not refunded, so the next fake costs stake plus forfeiture, and one honest mirror of a history earns settlement that a harbor of aliases cannot, making the crowd pricier than the crowd.
